b.sound: The most iconic section of the canyon is the Valley of Castles, famous for its red sandstone formations.
The most iconic section of the canyon is the Valley of Castles, famous for its white marble formations.
The Shahryn River runs through the canyon and eventually flows into Lake Balkhahsh, one of the world’s largest lakes.
The Shahryn Glacier runs through the canyon and eventually flows into Lake Balkhahsh, one of the world’s largest lakes.
Sharyn Canyon supports rare wildlife, including the Pallas’s cat, a wild cat native to Central Asia.

hint.label: Silk Road
text: The Silk Road was a huge network of trade routes connecting East Asia with Europe and the Middle East and stretched for over 35,000 kilometres.

atoms.a: Samarkand in Uzbekistan is one of the world’s oldest cities and is famous for its blue-tiled mosaics.
Its long history is linked to the Silk Road, where traders came to Samarkand to trade valuable goods such as silk, spices and precious stones.
These goods were carried from city to city by camel caravans, which are still sometimes used as a form of transport today.
Tourists can visit Registan Square: a historic public square where people once gathered and traded.

atoms.b: The Darvaza Gas Crater, also known as the Door to ((++Hell Heaven)), is a huge natural gas crater located in Turkmenistan. It has been ((++burning freezing)) continuously since 1971, when scientists set fire to it to stop gas from escaping.
atoms.sound: The Dar-vahzah Gas Crater, also known as the Door to Hell, is a huge natural gas crater located in Turkmenistan. It has been burning continuously since 1971, when scientists set fire to it to stop gas from escaping.

atoms.b: The crater is about 30 metres deep and more than 60 metres wide, while the burning gas inside can reach temperatures of over ((++1,000_°C 30_°C)).
Despite being in the middle of the Karakum Desert, it still attracts around ((++10,000 100)) tourists each year.
atoms.sound: Despite being in the middle of the Kahrahkoom Desert, it still attracts around 10,000 tourists each year.

atoms.text: The Aral Sea is a huge area covering much of Central Asia. However, since rivers were redirected to provide water for farming in the 1960s, the Aral Sea has lost about 90% of its water.
In Uzbekistan, most of the South Aral Sea has dried up completely! This has created the vast Aralkum Desert, which is littered with abandoned boats.
atoms.sound: In Uzbekistan, most of the South Aral Sea has dried up completely! This has created the vast Aral koom Desert, which is littered with abandoned boats.

atoms.text: In contrast, the Kok-Aral Dam in Kazakhstan was built in 2005 to stop the North Aral Sea from shrinking. Since then, the water level has risen significantly, and many fish have returned.
atoms.sound: In contrast, the Coke Aral Dam in Kazakhstan was built in 2005 to stop the North Aral Sea from shrinking. Since then, the water level has risen significantly, and many fish have returned.
